semanticDifferences: React Aria's trigger and overlay were siblings wired through context; Base UI links them with `Dialog.createHandle()` + a detached `Dialog.Trigger` (the composition Base UI documents for that exact shape). The handle lives in the trigger and reaches the overlay through a private context, so a standalone `<ModalOverlay>` still creates its own handle and no public export changed.

`isDismissable` (default false) has no Base UI prop; it is carried by `disablePointerDismissal={!isDismissable}` on the Root, which also blocks focus-out dismissal for non-modal dialogs (documented Base UI behaviour; React Aria's prop only covered outside presses).

`isKeyboardDismissDisabled` has no Base UI prop: Escape is vetoed through `eventDetails.cancel()` when the reason is 'escape-key'; `shouldCloseOnInteractOutside` is reconstructed from `eventDetails.event.target` for the 'outside-press' and 'focus-out' reasons.

Base UI's `Dialog.Popup` is itself `role="dialog"`; the adopted payload already renders React Aria's dialog element inside it. The popup's role is therefore removed (role={undefined}) so the DOM keeps exactly one named dialog element — Base UI's `Dialog.Title`/`Description` parts are not used by this payload, so a popup-owned role would have been nameless (axe `aria-dialog-name`).

Enter/exit phases are attribute driven. React Aria applied classes while `isEntering`/`isExiting` were true; `data-starting-style` in Base UI lasts a single frame (the enter animation would be cancelled when the class is removed), so entries key off `data-open` and exits off `data-ending-style`, the same pattern the landed tooltip unit uses. The render props consumers receive are derived: `isExiting` = data-ending-style phase, `isEntering` = open && !ending.

Base UI portals nothing on the server (verified: `<ModalOverlay isOpen>` renders "" with renderToString, exactly like the frozen React Aria baseline), so SSR output is unchanged: the trigger is server-rendered with aria-expanded=false and the overlay mounts on the client.

Initial focus differs by design: React Aria focused the dialog element, Base UI focuses the first tabbable element inside the popup (the popup itself on touch). Focus containment, Escape handling (topmost dialog first) and focus return to the trigger are unchanged; `Popup.initialFocus` can restore the old behaviour if a consumer wants it.

Base UI adds two invisible internals React Aria had no equivalent for: an InternalBackdrop (`div[role=presentation][data-base-ui-inert]`) when modal, and focus-guard spans inside the backdrop. Neither is a slot or affects geometry.

React Aria published `--visual-viewport-height` (and page size) on the modal element; the adopted class `max-h-[calc(var(--visual-viewport-height)-var(--modal-pt)-var(--modal-pb))]` reads it. Base UI has no equivalent, so modal.tsx restores that single variable from `window.visualViewport` (falling back to `document.documentElement.clientHeight`, ignoring pinch-zoomed updates, `0px` on the server — React Aria's own SSR value). `--visual-viewport-width`/`--page-*` were not restored because no adopted class reads them.
`AlertDialog` is not used by this unit; per docs/alert-dialog.json its parts are the Dialog parts verbatim, so nothing here would change if one were added.

migrationRecord.publicComponent: application/modals/modal.tsx (DialogTrigger, ModalOverlay, Modal, Dialog), application/slideout-menus/slideout-menu.tsx (ModalOverlay, Modal, Dialog, SlideoutMenu with .Trigger/.Content/.Header/.Footer), application/app-navigation nav parts (NavAccountMenu, NavAccountCard, MobileNavigationHeader, NavItemBase, NavButton, SidebarNavigationSlim)
migrationRecord.existingUntitledUiBehavior: React Aria composition: `<DialogTrigger>` provided the overlay state through context and cloned/press-wired the first child; `ModalOverlay` rendered the dimmed, centring underlay (isDismissable/isKeyboardDismissDisabled live here); `Modal` rendered the panel; `Dialog` rendered the `section[role=dialog]` content and exposed `{close}` to its children function. The nav parts used React Aria `Button`/`Pressable`/`Link`/`Popover`/`useFocusManager`, anchored the account menu to the whole card and did arrow-key focus movement inside it.
migrationRecord.canonicalBehavioralContract: A trigger with aria-expanded/aria-haspopup opens one visible overlay; Escape closes the topmost overlay and returns focus to the trigger; focus is contained while modal; outside presses dismiss only when `isDismissable`; the trigger's open state stays reachable from render props (`isEntering`/`isExiting`/`state`, `{close}`); the account menu keeps ArrowUp/ArrowDown tabbable wrapping; the dialog element keeps its accessible name (aria-label or aria-labelledby).
migrationRecord.baseUiCompositionChosen: Dialog: `Dialog.Root(handle)` > `Dialog.Portal` > `Dialog.Backdrop` (the payload's overlay classes) > the payload's `Modal` = `Dialog.Popup` (role stripped) > the payload's `Dialog` (useRender `section[role=dialog]`). Trigger side: `Dialog.Trigger handle={…} render={<FirstChild/>}`. Slideout: identical with its own slide classes (considered `Drawer`, rejected — see baseUiPrimitives). Popover (nav): `Popover.Root` > `Popover.Trigger` (chevron button / avatar button) > `Popover.Portal` > `Popover.Positioner (anchor=card ref)` > `Popover.Popup role={undefined}` > `NavAccountMenu` (section role=dialog). mobile-header composes the Dialog parts directly because its overlay/panel classes are unrelated to the modal's.
migrationRecord.whyNotOneToOne: React Aria's `DialogTrigger` puts the trigger and the overlay in one state provider that also clones the trigger element. Base UI has no single part that does both, and its popup parts must be composed `Portal > Backdrop/Positioner > Popup`; the visible contract (aria-expanded + one visible overlay, Escape/focus/cancel semantics) is preserved by shipping the same part names over Base UI primitives, with the trigger wired by `Dialog.createHandle()` because the payload's children are siblings. Two invisible differences are accepted and documented above: Base UI's InternalBackdrop + focus guards, and the initial-focus target.

No console errors in any probe.
